mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and increase S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the 20-day periods following high UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP and housing starts indicate strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 60-day periods following GDP and housing starts growth.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 20-day periods following high INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 20-day periods following a FEDFUNDS decrease.

mechanism_narrative: High employment and low unemployment indicate a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 60-day periods following high PAYEMS and low UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 5-day periods following high RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rate in a late-cycle expansion indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the 20-day periods following low UNRATE in late-cycle expansion.
